# Writing akceo decks

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_guide.py from docs/agent/, docs/syntax.md and the demo deck. Edit those and run it again. -->

This guide is for akceo 0.2.1.

akceo builds a slide deck from one Markdown file into one HTML file that loads nothing from
outside, so it opens from disk, offline, or as an email attachment.

It isn't a free-form HTML tool, and it reads only its own small set of Markdown. A deck holds no
raw HTML: `<` and `&` show as text. Each slide has one of six layouts, and each layout takes only
certain kinds of content. Many mistakes stop the build with a message that names the file, the
slide and a line: an unknown key, content the layout doesn't take, a missing image, or a diagram
Mermaid can't parse. Not every mistake does. Markdown that akceo doesn't support shows as plain
text, with no error; the recipes below list what to avoid.

## How to work

1. Pick each slide's layout first: `title`, `bullets`, `split`, `steps`, `table` or `image`.
2. Write the deck.
3. Run `akceo check deck.md` after every edit, and fix what it reports. It stops at the first
   problem, so run it again until it prints `ok`.
4. Run `akceo build deck.md` to write `deck.html` next to the deck.
5. `ok` means akceo found nothing wrong, not that every slide looks right. Have the built page
   looked at, above all the slides with a diagram, which can show an error only when the page
   opens, and the dense ones, which can overflow.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `akceo check deck.md` | Runs every check, diagrams included, and writes nothing |
| `akceo check --json deck.md` | The same, with the result as JSON |
| `akceo build deck.md` | Writes `deck.html`. `-o` names another file, and `--theme` overrides the deck's theme |
| `akceo themes` | Lists the built-in themes |
| `akceo docs` | Prints where this guide is. `--print` prints the guide itself |
| `akceo init` | Adds a section to `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` in a folder that points agents to this guide |

`akceo check --json` prints one JSON object, and exits 0 when `ok` is true and 1 when it isn't:

| Field | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | `true` when akceo found nothing wrong |
| `deck` | The deck's path, as given |
| `slides` | The number of slides, or `null` when there's an error |
| `errors` | The problem found, or an empty list. Checking stops at the first problem, so there's one at most |

Each error has:

| Field | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | The kind of problem, such as `block-missing`; the Error codes section lists them all |
| `message` | What's wrong, without the file and line |
| `file`, `line`, `slide` | Where the problem is, usually in the deck. Each is `null` when it doesn't apply |
| `in` | The file and line inside another file the slide uses, such as its diagram, or `null` |
| `text` | The line `akceo check` prints |

Fields may be added later, but none is renamed or removed. A mistake in the command itself, such
as an unknown option, exits 2 and prints how to use the command, not JSON.

## Deck syntax

A deck is one Markdown file. It starts with a config block. Then come the slides, each one after
a line that holds only `---`.

```markdown
title: My Talk
theme: paper
images: ./img

---

layout: title
kicker: Welcome

# My Talk

---

kicker: Agenda

## What we'll cover

- First thing
- Second thing
```

Mistakes stop the build with a message that names the file, the slide and a line. The line is
the key's own when a key is wrong, and the block's first line when a block, or a link in it, is
wrong. A problem with the slide as a whole, such as a missing heading or image, names the line
the slide starts on. Examples are an unknown key, a key on the wrong layout, a missing heading,
or content the layout doesn't use.

### Config block

The config block is everything before the first `---`. It may hold only `key: value` lines.

| Key | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | Page title shown in the browser tab | The file name without `.md` |
| `description` | A sentence or two about the deck, for search results and link previews | None |
| `url` | The page's full address once it's published, starting `https://` or `http://` | None |
| `icon` | Image for the browser tab, relative to the deck: PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG. PNG, JPEG and WebP are shrunk to fit 256 pixels; SVG stays sharp at any size. Safari shows the icon only when the page is served from a website, not when it's opened from a file. | None |
| `theme` | Built-in theme name, or a path to a `.css` file relative to the deck | `midnight` |
| `images` | Folder to read slide images from, relative to the deck | The deck's folder |
| `image-frame` | `no` puts every image straight on the slide, with no panel behind it. See [Images](#images). | `yes` |

`description` and `url` are for a deck published on the web. `url` tells search engines which
address is the page's own. Either key also adds the Open Graph tags that link previews read,
with the deck's `title`. None of the three loads anything, so the page still opens from disk.

### Slides

A slide starts with `key: value` header lines. Then comes a blank line, then the content.

Keys are lowercase. They end at the first line that isn't a key or an [author
note](#author-notes), so a key written after the blank line, or in capitals, such as `Kicker:`,
shows on the slide as text.

#### Slide keys

| Key | Layouts | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | all | `title`, `bullets`, `split`, `steps`, `table` or `image`. Default `bullets`. |
| `kicker` | all | Small uppercase label above the heading. |
| `meta` | title | A line of text under the title. |
| `image` | split, image | Image file, relative to the `images` folder. Leave it out to show a dashed placeholder while the image doesn't exist yet. |
| `image-alt` | split, image | Alt text for the image. |
| `image-max` | split, image | Longest side in pixels after shrinking: a whole number of at most nine digits 0-9. Default `2400`. |
| `image-crop` | split, image | Keep only part of the image: `left, top, right, bottom` in pixels, such as `120, 80, 920, 580`, each a whole number of at most nine digits 0-9. Commas or spaces separate the numbers. See [Images](#images). |
| `image-wide` | split | `yes` gives the image the wider column. |
| `image-frame` | split, image | `yes` or `no` for this slide's image, overriding the deck's `image-frame`. |
| `dim-last-column` | table | `yes` shows the last column in muted text. |
| `style-h1`, `style-h2`, `style-lead`, `style-ul`, `style-ol`, `style-sub` | all | Inline CSS for that element, for one-off spacing fixes. `style-sub` applies to the paragraph, which is the caption on an `image` slide. It can't reference files or URLs. |

#### Layouts

| Layout | Shows | Takes | Requires |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | A centered title | `#` heading | `#` heading |
| `bullets` | A heading and a list | `##` heading, `>` lead, `-` list, paragraph | `##` heading |
| `split` | An image left, text right | `##` heading, any number of `###` phases and `-` lists, one `*note*` | `##` heading |
| `steps` | A numbered sequence | `##` heading, paragraph, `1.` list | `##` heading, `1.` list |
| `table` | A table | `##` heading, `\|` table | `##` heading, `\|` table |
| `image` | An image filling the slide, with an optional heading above it and caption below it | `##` heading, paragraph | nothing |

Each kind of content may appear once per slide. A layout shows its content in the order of the
Takes column, whatever order the slide gives it in: in `bullets`, a paragraph written above the
list still shows below it. In the `split` layout, phases and lists may repeat and render in the
order written. There, the note always renders last. In the `image` layout, the paragraph is a
caption: smaller muted text, centered under the image.

### Blocks

| Write | Get |
| --- | --- |
| `# Text` | Title heading (`title` layout) |
| `## Text` | Slide heading |
| `### Name` and a line under it | A phase: a name and a one-line description (`split` layout). The description is optional; a blank line or another block right after the name leaves it out. |
| `- item` | Bulleted list |
| `1. item` | Numbered list |
| `> text` | Lead: larger text. Consecutive `>` lines join into one. |
| `\| a \| b \|` | Table row. The first row is the header. A `\| --- \| --- \|` row after it is skipped. |
| `*text*` | Note: a whole line in single asterisks (`split` layout) |
| Anything else | Paragraph. Consecutive lines join into one. |

Table cells split on `|`. A pipe inside backticks stays in its cell, as in `` `a|b` ``. Anywhere
else, write `\|` for a literal pipe.

Two rules join lines:

- A line indented by two spaces joins the line above with a space. Use it to wrap long list
  items.
- A trailing `\` joins the next line with a hard line break.

### Author notes

A line whose first non-space characters are `//` is a note to yourself. It never reaches the
page. Use it for reminders such as "this becomes a split once the diagram exists".

```markdown
## Integrations
// TODO: add the partner API row once it ships
| Path | Returns |
```

A note can go anywhere: in the config block, among a slide's header lines, or between the
lines of a list or paragraph. The content around it reads as if the note weren't there, so a
note between two list items doesn't split the list. A slide that holds only notes is skipped,
which lets you stub a slide you haven't written yet. There's no escape, so a line of slide text
can't start with `//`.

### Inline markup

| Write | Get |
| --- | --- |
| `**text**` | Bold |
| `***text***` | Bold in the theme's `--strong` color |
| `==text==` | Accent color |
| `((text))` | Muted text, shown in parentheses |
| `` `text` `` | Code. Markup inside it stays literal. |
| `[text](url)` | A link. The text can carry the other marks. |

Characters like `<` and `&` are escaped, so raw HTML shows as text.

A link goes to one of these, and anything else stops the build:

- an `https:` or `http:` address, or a `mailto:` address. These always open in a new tab, so
  the deck stays open.
- a slide in the deck, as `#N`, such as `[back to the plan](#3)`. The slide must exist.

A URL can't contain a space, a quote or `)`. Write `%20` for a space and `%29` for `)`. The
link text can't contain `]`; a link written with one shows as plain text.
Clicking a link follows it without changing the slide.

`#N` counts the slides on the page. A slide that holds only [author notes](#author-notes) is
skipped and doesn't count, so when you fill one in, every slide after it is numbered one higher.
Check the `#N` links to those slides.

### Images

The `split` and `image` layouts embed their image in the page.

- **PNG, JPEG and WebP** are turned upright using their EXIF orientation, cropped to
  `image-crop` if it's set, then shrunk so the longest side is at most `image-max`. Smaller
  images are never enlarged. JPEG and WebP are re-saved at quality 90.
- **SVG** is embedded unchanged.
- **Mermaid** diagrams in a `.mmd` file are drawn as SVG by the page when it opens. akceo
  includes Mermaid, so nothing else needs installing. See [Mermaid diagrams](#mermaid-diagrams).
  An image inside a diagram can be a file too; see [Images in diagrams](#images-in-diagrams).

Other formats stop the build, and so does an image akceo can't process, such as one with
damaged EXIF data.

`image-crop` gives the part of the image to keep, in pixels counted from the top-left corner of
the image as it appears, upright. `left` and `top` are the first column and row kept; `right` and
`bottom` are the edges just past the last ones. So `image-crop: 120, 80, 920, 580` keeps an 800
by 500 area, and `0, 0, W, H` keeps all of a W by H image. A photo stored sideways with an EXIF
orientation counts in its upright size, which may not be the size other tools report.

A crop that goes past the image's edge stops the build and gives the image's size, and its
stored size too when EXIF turned it. A crop on an SVG or a Mermaid diagram also stops the build.

#### Mermaid diagrams

The build checks each diagram's syntax with Mermaid's own parser, so a mistake stops the build
with Mermaid's message and the line in the `.mmd` file:

```
akceo: deck.md:40: slide 6: flow.mmd:3: Parse error: Expecting 'PE', 'TAGEND', ... got 'SQE'
```

`akceo check deck.md` runs the same checks without writing a file.

A diagram can't load or link to anything outside the deck. Links may only point at a `#` anchor,
such as `#5` for slide 5. An image must be a file that the build puts into the diagram (see
[Images in diagrams](#images-in-diagrams)) or a `data:` URI. Anything else loaded counts as
outside, including a relative path in label HTML: it would point at a file next to `deck.html`,
which is gone once the deck is copied. The build stops, naming the line, on:

- links: `click` (including `href`), a class diagram's `link`, a sequence diagram's `link` and
  `links`, C4's `$link=`, and `<a href=…>` in a label.
- images: a URL in an image shape's `img:` (`b@{ img: … }`), and `src`, `srcset` and similar
  attributes in label HTML.
- CSS: `url(…)` and `@import`, whether in `themeCSS` in the front matter or an `%%{init}%%` line,
  or in a `style=` in a label. `url(#id)`, which points inside the diagram, is fine.

A URL that is only text in a label is fine. `%%` comments aren't checked.

This check is there to give a clear message. The page itself carries a Content-Security-Policy that
makes the browser refuse any outside load, so nothing the check misses can reach the network.

A diagram longer than 50,000 characters stops the build too. That's Mermaid's limit: past it,
Mermaid draws a notice instead of the diagram.

The page then draws each diagram as inline SVG when it opens. A few mistakes only show up at
that point, such as an invalid date in a `gantt` chart. Those don't stop the build. The slide
shows Mermaid's message in place of the diagram.

A deck with at least one diagram carries a compressed copy of Mermaid, which adds about 2.4 MB
to the file. A deck without diagrams doesn't. The page unpacks Mermaid when it opens. Unpacking
and Mermaid itself together need Chrome or Edge 98, Firefox 113 or Safari 16.4, or newer. In an
older browser, each diagram shows a message in its place. Mermaid's Font Awesome icons
(`fa:fa-car`) don't show, because the page loads no outside stylesheets.

##### Images in diagrams

An image shape's `img:` can name an image file, relative to the `.mmd` file's folder. Write it
the way Mermaid takes any value in shape data: in double or single quotes, or bare.

```
flowchart LR
  a --> b@{ img: "screenshot.png", label: "The new form", w: 300, constraint: "on" }
```

The build reads the file and puts it into the diagram as a `data:` URI, the same way it embeds a
slide's image: PNG, JPEG and WebP are turned upright and re-saved, and SVG goes in unchanged. A
missing file stops the build with its path and the line in the `.mmd` file. A `data:` URI is
used as it is.

The build asks Mermaid which nodes have an image, so `@{ img: … }` inside a label is only text.
It then finds each image in the `.mmd` file to replace it. An image Mermaid reads that akceo
can't find there, such as one given through a YAML anchor, stops the build naming its node.
Write it on one line, as above.

Mermaid stretches an image to fill its node's box. The box takes the node's `w` and `h`, and the
image's own size in pixels for a side the node doesn't set. With `constraint: "on"` and only `w`
or `h`, Mermaid works out the other side from the image's shape instead. So to keep an image in
proportion, set `w` with `constraint: "on"`, as above, or set both. A node with a label is at
least 120 pixels wide.

When the node sets `w` or `h`, the image is shrunk to twice that, which stays sharp on a
high-density screen. When it sets neither, the image keeps its size. An image that several nodes
use is sized for the largest.

Two options after a `#` on the path change that. Join them with `&`, and quote a path that has
any:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `crop=left,top,right,bottom` | Keep only part of the image, in pixels, as `image-crop` does for a slide's image. |
| `max=pixels` | Shrink the image so its longest side is at most this many pixels, instead of fitting it to twice `w` and `h`. In a node without a label that sets neither, Mermaid draws it at this size. Not for SVG: set the node's `w` and `h` instead. |

```
flowchart LR
  a --> b@{ img: "screenshot.png#crop=0,0,1200,800&max=600", w: 300, constraint: "on" }
```

A file whose name contains `#` can't be used, and neither can a path that's only options, such
as `img: "#max=300"`.

Each image counts toward Mermaid's 50,000-character limit on the diagram, at about four
characters for every three bytes of the image, and an image used twice counts twice. Over the
limit, the build stops and lists how much each image uses. Crop or shrink the largest, or split
the diagram.

#### Frames

By default an image sits on a panel in the theme's `--figure-bg` color, with a shadow. Both
built-in themes use white, which suits screenshots and photos. `image-frame: no` drops the
panel, so the image sits straight on the slide. Set it in the config block for the whole deck,
or on one `split` or `image` slide. A slide's setting wins over the deck's.

A Mermaid diagram with no frame is drawn in the deck theme's colors, so it matches the slides:

- node fill: `--line`
- node border: `--accent`
- text: `--text`
- arrows: `--muted`
- font: `--font`

A diagram in a frame keeps Mermaid's own default colors, which read well on white. Mermaid
also needs to know whether the background is dark. akceo works that out from `--bg` when it is
a hex color such as `#0b0f16`. Other color formats leave Mermaid to guess. For finer control,
start the `.mmd` file with Mermaid's own `%%{init: …}%%` line.

The frame setting doesn't change the image itself. A screenshot with a white background still
shows white.

A `split` or `image` slide with no `image:` line shows a dashed box where the image will go, so
you can set up the slide before the image exists. An `image:` that names a missing file still stops the
build.

### Themes

A theme is a CSS file. akceo adds it after its own layout rules, so a theme sets the tokens below
and can also override any layout rule. A theme that leaves out any token stops the build, and
the message lists the missing ones. The three link tokens are the exception: they're needed only
when the deck has a link, so a theme written before links existed still builds a deck without
any.

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--bg` | Page background, and the numbers in `steps` |
| `--line` | Table rules and the border of an image placeholder |
| `--text` | Body text |
| `--muted` | Paragraphs, notes, the meta line, `((dimmed))` text, the slide count and the key hint |
| `--strong` | Bold text in lists and the first table column, phase names, `***strong***` |
| `--accent` | Kickers, list markers, `==accent==`, table headers, the progress bar |
| `--accent2` | Code |
| `--link` | Link text. Needed only when the deck has a link. |
| `--link-hover` | Link text on hover and keyboard focus. Needed only when the deck has a link. |
| `--link-underline` | Link underline, as a `text-decoration` value such as `underline 1px` or `none`. Needed only when the deck has a link. |
| `--figure-bg` | Background behind `split` and `image` images |
| `--figure-shadow` | Shadow under `split` and `image` images (a `box-shadow` value) |
| `--font` | Body font stack |
| `--mono` | Code font stack |

A comment on a theme's first line is its description in `akceo themes`. The page's
Content-Security-Policy stops it loading anything from outside, so a web font or an `@import` in a
theme never shows. Use fonts installed on the machine you present from, or embed one as a
`data:` URI in an `@font-face` rule.

### Error codes

`akceo check` stops at the first problem and names its file, line and slide. Each problem also
has a code, which `akceo check --json` reports, so an agent can act on the kind of problem without
reading the message. A code is never renamed or reused.

| Code | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `file-not-found` | The deck, a theme, an image, the icon or a diagram doesn't exist |
| `file-unreadable` | A file exists but can't be read, such as when permission is denied |
| `file-not-utf8` | The deck, a theme or a diagram isn't UTF-8 text |
| `file-unwritable` | The built page, the viewer or a file `akceo init` writes can't be written |
| `deck-control-character` | The deck has a control character in it |
| `deck-no-slides` | The deck has no slides |
| `config-not-key-value` | A line in the config block isn't `key: value` |
| `key-unknown` | A config key or slide key akceo doesn't know |
| `layout-unknown` | A `layout:` that isn't one of the six |
| `key-wrong-layout` | A slide key that only works with other layouts |
| `value-not-yes-or-no` | A yes-or-no key with another value |
| `value-not-pixels` | `image-max`, or `max=` in a diagram's `img:`, isn't a positive whole number |
| `crop-invalid` | `image-crop`, or `crop=` in a diagram's `img:`, isn't four whole numbers |
| `crop-empty` | A crop that keeps nothing |
| `crop-past-edge` | A crop past the image's edge |
| `image-option-unsupported` | A crop or `max=` on an SVG image, or `image-crop` on a diagram |
| `url-invalid` | `url:` isn't a full `https://` or `http://` address |
| `style-url` | A `style-…` key uses `url()` or `image-set()` |
| `block-not-in-layout` | Content the slide's layout doesn't take |
| `block-repeated` | A second block of a kind the layout takes only once |
| `block-missing` | A block the layout needs, such as the `##` heading |
| `link-split` | A link's URL runs onto the next line |
| `link-past-last-slide` | A `#N` link past the last slide |
| `link-target-invalid` | A link that isn't to `https:`, `http:`, `mailto:` or `#N` |
| `image-format-unsupported` | An image that isn't PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG, such as a GIF |
| `image-damaged` | An image file that can't be decoded |
| `image-too-large` | An image over Pillow's size limit, about 179 million pixels; shrink it |
| `diagram-syntax` | Mermaid can't parse the diagram |
| `diagram-too-long` | A diagram over Mermaid's size limit |
| `diagram-loads-outside` | A diagram that loads or links to anything outside the deck |
| `diagram-timeout` | Mermaid took too long to check the diagram |
| `img-unlocated` | akceo can't tell where a node's `img:` is written in the diagram |
| `img-no-path` | An `img:` that starts with `#` |
| `img-unquoted` | An `img:` with options that isn't in quotes |
| `img-option-invalid` | An `img:` option that's unknown or given twice |
| `theme-unknown` | A theme name that isn't built in |
| `theme-closes-style` | A theme with `</style` in it |
| `theme-missing-tokens` | A theme that leaves out a token it needs, including the link tokens for a deck with links |
| `init-not-folder` | `akceo init` was given something that isn't a folder |
| `init-link-outside` | `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` links to a file outside the folder |
| `init-broken-link` | `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` links to a file that doesn't exist |

## Deck recipes

The syntax says what a deck can hold. These say what works.

- **Pick the layout before the words.** `bullets` is the default. `split` suits a diagram or
  screenshot with commentary, and `image` gives one the whole slide. `akceo check` names the
  blocks a layout takes when a slide has one it doesn't.
- **Write only akceo's Markdown.** The blocks and marks in the syntax tables are all there is.
  Code fences, nested lists, `*` or `+` bullets and `####` headings show as plain text, and
  `akceo check` doesn't flag them. A list is one level deep: an indented `- item` joins the item
  above it.
- **Keys go first, in lowercase.** A slide's keys end at the first line that isn't a key or a
  `//` note, so a key written after the blank line, or in capitals, shows on the slide as text.
- **An image that doesn't exist yet:** leave out `image:`, and the slide shows a dashed box where
  it will go. Don't make up a file name, because a missing file stops the build.
- **Diagrams:** put each one in its own `.mmd` file and use `image: name.mmd`. On a dark theme,
  `image-frame: no` draws it in the theme's colors.
- **Screenshots:** `image-crop` keeps only the part that matters, which reads better than
  shrinking the whole screen.
- **Notes to yourself:** a line that starts with `//` never reaches the page. Use it for TODOs,
  and for a slide you haven't written yet: a slide that holds only notes is skipped. It doesn't
  count in slide numbers either, so filling it in later moves every `#N` link to a slide after it.
- **Long list items:** indent the next line by two spaces to continue an item. A trailing `\`
  is a hard line break.
- **`style-…` keys** are a last resort for spacing. If you reach for one often, the slide wants
  a different layout.
- **Dense slides:** akceo can't tell yet whether text overflows a slide. Past about 100 words,
  have the built page looked at, or split the slide.

## A worked example

This is `examples/demo/deck.md` from akceo's repository. It uses every layout. Its diagram, `flow.mmd`, follows it, and `flow.svg` is a plain SVG image.

```markdown
title: Akceo demo
theme: midnight

---

layout: title
kicker: Akceo demo
meta: Markdown in, one self-contained HTML file out

# Decks at the speed of text

---

kicker: Why

## Slides are structured text

// Author note: lines that start with // never reach the page.
- Write in **Markdown**, keep the deck in git, and review it in a diff.
- Build to a **single HTML file** with images embedded and no external assets.
- Open it anywhere: a browser, offline, or from an email attachment.

This slide uses the ***bullets*** layout: a heading, a list and a closing paragraph.

---

kicker: Inline markup
style-lead: max-width:40ch;margin-bottom:3vh

## A small set of marks

> A lead line sets the tone and can carry an ==accent==.

- `**bold**` gives **bold**, and `***strong***` gives ***strong***.
- `==accent==` gives ==accent==, and `((dim))` gives ((a muted aside)).
- Backticks give code, and markup inside them stays literal: `==like this==`.
- `[text](url)` links out, as to the [format reference](https://github.com/LunarCommand/akceo/blob/main/docs/syntax.md),
  in a new tab. `[text](#7)` jumps to a slide, such as [the image layout](#7).
- Indent a line by two spaces to wrap a long item across lines
  in the source without breaking it on the slide.

## One command,\
one file

### write
slides in deck.md, then pick a theme

### build
akceo build deck.md

### present
open deck.html and press F for full screen

*Images are shrunk and embedded at build time.*

---

layout: steps
kicker: Getting started

## From zero to a deck

Install once. After that it's a write, build, present loop.

1. Install: `uv tool install akceo`
2. Write `deck.md`: a config block, then slides separated by `---`.
3. Build: `akceo build deck.md`
4. Present: open `deck.html` and use the arrow keys.

---

layout: table
kicker: Reference
dim-last-column: yes

## Six layouts

| Layout | Best for | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **title** | Opening and section slides | `#` heading, kicker, meta line |
| **bullets** | Most slides | `##` heading, lead, list, paragraph |
| **split** | A diagram with commentary | image, `##` heading, phases, lists, note |
| **steps** | A sequence | `##` heading, paragraph, numbered list |
| **table** | Comparisons | `##` heading, table |
| **image** | A diagram on its own | image, kicker, `##` heading, caption |
```
